sections.title: Climate
sections.filled: Across the surrounding basin of about 16,336 km², rainfall averages about 588 mm a year, moderately seasonal, with July the wettest month. Temperatures there average 7.5 °C, from -4.5 °C in January to 18.1 °C in July. Its aridity index of 0.79 falls in the UNEP humid class. Its basin is warmer than 10 of the 12 basins around it.

sections.title: Land and geology
sections.filled: Across the basin, the land is very gently sloping on average (a mean slope of 1.9%), with topsoil that averages 43% sand, 39% silt and 18% clay (USDA texture class: loam). The underlying rock is mostly carbonate sedimentary rocks.

sections.title: About these figures
sections.filled: The elevation and ecoregion under Setting are for Lviv itself. The other figures describe the basin of about 16,336 km² that contains it, from global datasets. 3 measures are zero here and so have no percentile: Karst area, Permafrost extent, Wetland extent group 2. Elevation and distances are measured from the place's point in WHG, which may be the centre of a town rather than its shore or riverbank.
